input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: § 8.2 matches our preferred position exactly: automatic renewals are limited to successive twelve-month periods, Customer may opt out on only thirty days' written notice, and Vendor must send a renewal reminder sixty days beforehand — with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed, which is better than our ask. § 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of US CPI and three percent, with ninety days' notice and no increase on prepaid periods, meeting the preferred price-predictability requirement. No auto-renewal escalator or longer notice window appears elsewhere (searches for "renew" and "increase" return only §§ 8.1–8.3), and § 8.1's three-year term is the initial term, not a multi-year auto-renewal. No redline needed.
